title: Trans-species microRNAs from the parasitic plant Cuscuta campestris specifically avoid loading onto self Argonautes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked all three GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) archives GSE333156_RAW.tar (9.6 MB), GSE333470_RAW.tar (7.2 MB), GSE333475_RAW.tar (7.6 MB); 27 processed CSV files, 52,471-52,573 rows each, 1,418,274 rows total. Counted entities: 52,573 unique names per file, of which only 268 are mature microRNAs with an actual RNA sequence in the 'Locus or Sequence' column; the other 52,305 are small-RNA clusters given as genome coordinates only (e.g. Cuca_chr1:932453-932945). Computed the paper's own final loading score (median over replicates of log2(immunoprecipitate/input) in the tagged-Argonaute line minus the same ratio in the untagged Col-0 control): 190 microRNAs have it for AGO1, 192 for AGO2, 189 for both. Measured replicate agreement (Spearman) and the fraction of variance explained by the 5' nucleotide alone.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biology (primary transcript timing, Dicer-Like 1 requirement, duplex accumulation in the parasite), the microRNA annotation provenance (miRBase v22 filtering plus Cerda et al. Cuscuta annotation), and the wet-lab design. The paper's supplementary file list was not retrievable from Europe PMC (request timed out), so supplementary tables were not inspected.

a1_downloadable.note: All three GEO series are public, no login; processed CSVs sit inside small RAW.tar files on the NCBI FTP site and downloaded on the first try.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: log2_ratio (immunoprecipitate over input) is already a column per replicate; the paper's final score needs one subtraction of the Col-0 control column and a median over three replicates - arithmetic on existing columns, not construction across sources.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequences are present for only 268 of 52,573 entities (the mature microRNAs). The 52,305 small-interfering-RNA entities are genome coordinates, so their input sequence would have to be pulled from the 1 Gb-scale Cuscuta campestris assembly GCA_052055255.1. Verified in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: KILLER. Only 189 microRNAs have a computable Argonaute-loading score for both AGO1 and AGO2 (190 and 192 separately); 268 microRNAs exist in total. Far below the ~1,500 rows for regression or ~400 for classification. Verified by counting in the files.

a4_units_stated.note: Units documented in the GEO sample records and consistent in the files: RPM21-24 (reads per million reads of 21-24 nucleotide length), log2 ratio, log10 abundance.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; loaded all 27 files into pandas in seconds.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: All files carry the same 52,573 (or 52,471) entity rows, consistent across series; the paper gives no competing explicit count to contradict, so nothing disagrees.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is a physical measurement: small-RNA sequencing read ratio between an antibody immunoprecipitate and its input, with an untagged-plant control subtracted. Not a model output. Verified against the GEO data-processing text.

existing_models.name: Support-vector-machine classifier of Argonaute-small-RNA affinity (bioRxiv 173575, 'Learning sequence patterns of AGO-sRNA affinity from high-throughput sequencing libraries')
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; search result states it learns 5' and 3' k-mer patterns plus length and first-nucleotide composition from Argonaute immunoprecipitation libraries.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved (abstract only seen through search snippet).

backbone.name: RNA-FM, an RNA language model (or a small k-mer logistic model, since the sequences are 20-24 nucleotides)
backbone.hardware: CPU only; 268 sequences of 24 nucleotides embed in seconds
backbone.licence: RNA-FM is open (MIT-style) but irrelevant here given the row count

integration.partner_dataset: Published Arabidopsis Argonaute immunoprecipitation small-RNA libraries (AGO1, AGO2, AGO4, AGO5, AGO7, AGO10) in GEO; miRBase v22 for mature sequences
integration.join_key: mature small-RNA sequence (exact string) and miRBase microRNA family name
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do the sequence rules that sort small RNAs into plant Argonautes generalise across species well enough to explain why a parasite's export-only microRNAs escape its own Argonautes?

controls.positive_control: The 5' nucleotide sorting rule must be recovered: in these files the median AGO2 enrichment is +7.33 for 5'-adenosine microRNAs versus -0.53 for 5'-guanosine, and AGO1 favours 5'-uridine (+3.39).
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the loading scores across microRNAs and confirm collapse; also train on 5' nucleotide alone, which already explains 37% (AGO1) and 41% (AGO2) of the variance.
controls.external_validation: Independent Arabidopsis Argonaute immunoprecipitation datasets from other labs, joined on mature microRNA sequence.

honest_claim_h3: Given only this paper's data, a model could claim at most: among 189 microRNAs annotated in Arabidopsis and Cuscuta campestris and detected in one lab's haustorial-interface tissue, sequence features predict relative enrichment in AGO1 versus AGO2 immunoprecipitates - a claim that the 5' nucleotide alone already largely supports.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a small RNA's sequence to predict which Argonaute protein will pick it up, and which escape loading entirely.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is one mature microRNA, 20-24 nucleotides, with its sequence, length, 5' nucleotide and origin category. Verified count: 268 microRNAs, of which 189 have usable loading scores.
plain_idea.predict: The loading score: log2 of the small-RNA sequencing read count in an Argonaute immunoprecipitate divided by the count in the matched input, with the untagged-plant control subtracted, measured in Arabidopsis stem tissue under a Cuscuta attachment.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Plant RNA-silencing labs and anyone designing small RNAs for crop protection would like a rule for which sequences load onto which Argonaute, and the parasite's export-only microRNAs would be a natural test of that rule - but 189 examples cannot support it.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict Argonaute loading (AGO1 versus AGO2 enrichment, or loaded versus avoided) from the 20-24 nucleotide small-RNA sequence, using the paper's immunoprecipitation sequencing data as labels. The data gives 189 labelled microRNAs - two orders of magnitude too few - and the 52,305 larger-n entities are small-interfering-RNA clusters with no sequence in the file and replicate Spearman agreement of only 0.14-0.20 on the loading score, i.e. the per-locus label is mostly noise.

effort.compute_note: Measured, not estimated: I downloaded all three archives, loaded all 27 CSV files (1,418,274 rows, ~130 MB) into pandas in a few seconds and built the loading-score table in one script.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct mature microRNAs that have a computable Argonaute enrichment score. The answer is 189 (190 for AGO1, 192 for AGO2), and that kills it in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: A5 fails hard: only 189 microRNAs carry the Argonaute-loading label, verified by counting in the downloaded files. A3 also fails for the one subset with large n - the 52,305 small-interfering-RNA entities are genome coordinates with no sequence, and their loading score barely reproduces between replicates (Spearman 0.14-0.20). On top of that, a single categorical feature, the 5' nucleotide, already explains 37-41% of the variance in the 189 usable rows, so the mapping is close to a four-row lookup table rather than a modelling problem. The data is clean, well documented and genuinely downloadable - it is simply a small, elegant mechanistic experiment, not a training set.
